model.name: Document / Record
model.purpose: Give an agent a format-neutral vocabulary for a governed information object whose identity outlives any file or carrier: captured as evidence of activity, carried through immutable versions and instantiations, made trustworthy by authenticity and integrity evidence, classified and accessed under authorized rules, and retained or destroyed only under disposition authority and holds.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the intellectual document or record and the recordkeeping facts an operator must know to create, inspect, trust, use, hold and dispose it. A document becomes a record when it is captured into a records system with identity, contextual metadata and controls; the same object may exist as an unmanaged document before capture. Aggregations of records (fonds, series, files as record sets) belong to the sibling archival-collection model. Agents, identifier schemes, calendars, message envelopes, warehouse locations and access-policy engines are referenced, not redefined.
in_scope: Stable identity of a document or record independent of storage path, filename or single bitstream
Declaration and capture as a record, including point-of-capture metadata and unique identifier assignment
Descriptive metadata (title, type, language, subject, coverage, documentary form) applied to the intellectual object
Documentary form, business classification and record series assignment as controls, not as scheme authoring
Immutable content versions and supersession between records or versions
Instantiations, renditions, formats, media types, extent, carriers and significant properties
Fixity, checksums, format registry keys and representation information needed for usability
Signatures, seals, timestamps, certificates and validation status on a specific version or instantiation
Content-credential manifests that bind provenance assertions to bytes, treated as an emerging authenticity mechanism
Creation, capture, registration, custody transfer, migration, conversion, use, hold and disposition events
Chain of custody, custodial register entries and distinction between owner, creator, custodian and rights holder
Retention schedules, triggers, contingent events, unscheduled-as-permanent treatment, disposition actions and evidence of destruction or transfer
Legal and administrative holds that suspend disposition
Access conditions, security or confidentiality marking, and PREMIS-style rights or licence statements attached to the object
Certified copies, extracts and use/reuse of a record or its metadata
Relationships of part/whole, format-of, version-of, replaces, references, requires and is-member-of a record set
Physical and analogue records as instantiations of the same intellectual object, without modelling conservation science in full
out_of_scope: Person, position, family and corporate-body identity and biography (agent sibling)
Organization master data beyond the issuer, owner or custodian role on this object
Archival fonds, series-as-aggregation, collection and record-set entities owned by WM-REC-015
Identifier scheme registration and syntax governance (naming sibling)
Calendar, working-day and time-zone rule engines (time sibling)
Message, email or conversation envelopes; attachments resolve here as records
Clinical document semantics (CDA, FHIR Composition) and bibliographic Work/Expression entities
Authoring of a business classification scheme, retention schedule or security policy; this model stores assignments and references
Full OAIS repository functions (ingest pipeline, designated-community watch, storage infrastructure) beyond the information-package facts on the record
Warehouse aisle/bin topology and facilities management
E-discovery process management, litigation case files and legal-matter master data beyond the hold that binds this record
Cryptographic key-management systems, PKI certificate authorities and timestamp authorities as operational services
Database-as-system or transactional information-system design; a snapshot or declared extract may be a record here

boundary_notes.distinction: ISO 15489 treats records regardless of structure or form and distinguishes creating information from capturing it as a record; this model takes the ISO capture-as-record lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-REC-015 archival fonds, collection or record set
boundary_notes.distinction: RiC-CM splits Record, Record Set, Record Part and Instantiation and says it does not physically manage instances; this model takes the RiC Record plus Instantiation split and leaves Record Set aggregations to WM-REC-015.
PREMIS Intellectual Entity maps to the governed object; representation, file and bitstream map to instantiations.
Dublin Core describes the resource and is a mix-in, not a recordkeeping control set.
C2PA is an emerging binding for media assets, not a substitute for records capture.

boundary_notes.neighbor: US Federal records law (44 U.S.C. 3301 / 36 CFR 1220.18)
boundary_notes.distinction: Defines Federal records, nonrecords, unscheduled and permanent treatment only for that jurisdiction; they are alignments, not global law.
Do not claim ISO, PREMIS, RiC, OAIS or C2PA conformance without a mapped profile.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Normative concepts and principles for records, metadata, records systems, records controls and processes of create, capture, classify, access, store, use, migrate and dispose, independent of form. Full text is paywalled on ISO; clause structure corroborated by identical national adoptions.

sources.title: ISO 23081 Metadata for records (ISO 23081-1:2017 principles; ISO 23081-2:2021 conceptual and implementation issues)
sources.relevance: Metadata must show that an object was managed as a record of events across its existence, supporting integrity, authenticity, reliability and usability in business context. Distinct from purely descriptive metadata.

sources.title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata, Version 3.0 — Hierarchical Listing of Semantic Units
sources.organization: Library of Congress / PREMIS Editorial Committee
sources.relevance: Entities: Intellectual Entity, Object (representation, file, bitstream), Event, Agent, Rights. Semantic units for identifiers, fixity, format, size, storage, signatureInformation, relationships and rights statements.

sources.title: Records in Contexts – Conceptual Model (RiC-CM) Version 1.0
sources.organization: International Council on Archives, Expert Group on Archival Description
sources.relevance: Entities include Record Resource (Record Set, Record, Record Part) and Instantiation, plus Agent, Activity, Event, Rule, Mandate, Date, Place. Record is discrete inscribed information; Instantiation is the carrier inscription. Explicitly not a physical-management or exchange format. Notes relationship and remaining differences with ISO 23081.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms
sources.organization: Dublin Core Metadata Initiative Usage Board
sources.relevance: Descriptive terms: identifier, title, type, format, language, creator, publisher, created, issued, modified, valid, hasVersion, isFormatOf, replaces, provenance, accessRights, license, rightsHolder. Mix-in for description, not a full records-control vocabulary.

sources.title: ISO 14721:2025 Space Data System Practices — Reference model for an Open Archival Information System (OAIS)
sources.relevance: Information packages SIP, AIP, DIP; Content Information plus Preservation Description Information (reference, provenance, context, fixity, access rights); ingest, archival storage, data management, access, dissemination, preservation planning. Alignment for long-term packages, not this model's operational archive.

sources.title: 36 CFR § 1220.18 — Definitions applicable to Federal records management
sources.organization: United States National Archives and Records Administration (as published in the e-CFR / LII)
sources.relevance: US Federal record, nonrecord, documentary materials, electronic record including required metadata, disposition, disposition authority, retention period, series, permanent, temporary, unscheduled (treat as permanent until scheduled), contingent records, personal files.

sources.title: C2PA Technical Specification — Content Credentials
sources.organization: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
sources.relevance: Signed manifest of assertions, claim and claim signature; hard binding (cryptographic hash of asset bytes) and optional soft binding (fingerprint or watermark). Emerging authenticity mechanism for digital assets; not a records-management standard.

sources.title: JIS X 0902-1:2019 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles (identical to ISO 15489-1:2016)
sources.relevance: Public identical adoption used to ground ISO 15489 clause 8 records controls (metadata schema, business classification, access/permission rules, disposition authority) and clause 9 processes, including capture assigning a unique identifier.

sources.title: eSignature FAQ — eIDAS electronic signatures, seals and qualified timestamps
sources.version_or_date: Guidance on Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS); page observed 2026-02-02
sources.relevance: Simple, advanced and qualified electronic signatures; qualified electronic seals; qualified electronic time stamps with presumption of date/time accuracy and integrity. Regional legal effect, not a global records model.

bundles.name: Identity and description
bundles.description: Establish what the object is: a durable identifier independent of files, its kind as document versus captured record, descriptive labels, documentary form and business classification assignment.
bundles.rationale: Persistent identity and kind/status/descriptive labels are grouped because they answer what the object is and whether it is under records controls, before any content, trust, custody, retention or access question can be posed.

layers.name: Persistent identity
layers.description: Bind a master identifier and any public identifiers to the intellectual object, not to a path, filename or single instantiation.

findings.name: Master and public identifiers
findings.description: A document or record requires an unambiguous identifier in a named scheme. Capture assigns a unique identifier. PREMIS requires objectIdentifierType plus objectIdentifierValue, repeatable across schemes. Dublin Core identifier is an unambiguous reference within a given context (ISBN, DOI, URN, HTTP URI). Identity priority is: authoritative master-system identifier; then a governed global IRI; then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. A date is not an identifier. Filename, URL path and storage key are location hints, not identity.

data_elements.name: Master-system identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the object as a typed identifier.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme or type
data_elements.description: Scheme or type of the identifier, as an enumerated code or IRI.

data_elements.name: Governed public IRI
data_elements.description: Governed global IRI denoting the object.

data_elements.name: Adopting-dimension UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Fallback UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.

data_elements.name: Human-readable document or record number
data_elements.description: Display document or record number as a string.

artifacts.name: Identifier register row
artifacts.description: The governed listing that binds scheme, value, assignment time and assigning system to this object.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by identifier scheme plus value, with assignment time and assigning system.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier and its scheme for this object?
answer_data: One typed identifier object: scheme IRI or code, identifier value, assigning system, assigned-at as RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z.

questions.text: Which public IRIs, document numbers, DOI/URN values or Dimension UUID/ULID values also denote this object, and which is correlatable versus display-only?
answer_data: Array of typed identifiers with role (public-iri, document-number, dimension-uuid) and correlation-use boolean.

questions.text: When was each identifier assigned, and is assignment time distinct from content creation time?
answer_data: For each identifier: assigned-at (event time) and recorded-at (observation/ingestion time), both RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z.

layers.name: Kind, status and descriptive labels
layers.description: Distinguish unmanaged documents from captured records and attach the descriptive facet used for discovery.

findings.name: Document versus captured record
findings.description: ISO 15489 applies to records regardless of structure or form and treats capture into a records system as the act that places identified information under records controls. RiC-CM defines a Record as discrete information content formed and inscribed, at least once, on any persistent recoverable carrier by an agent in the course of activity. US 36 CFR 1220.18 / 44 U.S.C. 3301 additionally excludes extra copies kept only for reference, library or museum materials for exhibit, and personal files. This model stores a record-status on the object: document-not-captured, captured-record, nonrecord-copy, or jurisdiction-specific Federal-record, rather than splitting into two meta-models.

data_elements.name: Record status
data_elements.description: Enumerated status: document-not-captured, captured-record, nonrecord-copy or jurisdiction-specific Federal-record.

data_elements.name: Jurisdictional record determination
data_elements.description: Structured determination that the object is a record under a named jurisdiction.

data_elements.name: Nonrecord or personal-file reason
data_elements.description: Enumerated excluding criterion where the object is a nonrecord, extra copy or personal file.

artifacts.name: Capture or nonrecord declaration
artifacts.description: The decision record that this object is or is not managed as a record, with authority and time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the object identifier plus determination time and deciding authority.

questions.text: Has this object been captured as a record, and under which jurisdiction or policy is that determination made?
answer_data: Enum record-status; optional jurisdiction code; policy or statute citation; determined-by agent ref; determined-at RFC 3339.

questions.text: If it is a nonrecord, extra copy or personal file, what is the excluding criterion?
answer_data: Enum nonrecord-reason plus free-text justification and ownership (agency versus individual).

questions.text: Who has authority to determine record status when systems or staff disagree?
answer_data: Agent or role ref plus cited mandate. For US Federal records, NARA determination is binding per the Federal Records Act as reflected in 36 CFR.

findings.name: Descriptive metadata and classification assignment
findings.description: Dublin Core supplies discovery labels: title, alternative, type, language, subject, coverage, creator, publisher, description. ISO 15489 records controls include a business classification scheme that links records to the activity context of creation; classification and indexing is a clause-9 process. RiC uses documentary form as a criterion for a record's boundary and for membership in a record set. This model stores assigned class, documentary form and index terms; it does not own the classification scheme vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Title
data_elements.description: Current title as a localized string.

data_elements.name: Type or genre
data_elements.description: Type or genre of the object, as an enumerated code or IRI.

data_elements.name: Language tag
data_elements.description: Language of the content as a BCP 47 tag.

data_elements.name: Documentary form type
data_elements.description: Documentary form as an IRI or code.

data_elements.name: Assigned business classification
data_elements.description: IRI reference to the assigned business classification class.

data_elements.name: Subject or index terms
data_elements.description: Subject or index terms as IRIs or strings.

artifacts.name: Descriptive metadata set
artifacts.description: The current authorized descriptive facet, including language of description and vocabulary sources.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One current authorized descriptive set per record identity.

questions.text: What is the current title, any alternative title, and the type or documentary form of this object?
answer_data: Localized title strings; alternative titles; type IRI or DCMI Type; documentary-form code.

questions.text: Which business classification, function or activity class is assigned, and from which scheme version?
answer_data: Scheme IRI and version, class code/IRI, assigned-by, assigned-at RFC 3339.

questions.text: What language(s) is the content in, and which subject or coverage terms apply?
answer_data: BCP 47 tags; subject IRIs preferred over literals; spatial/temporal coverage as Place or Period refs.

bundles.name: Content, representation and versioning
bundles.description: Describe the intellectual content state, its instantiations or renditions in particular formats and carriers, and the immutable version chain including supersession.
bundles.rationale: Instantiations/renditions and versioning/supersession are grouped because both separate the intellectual record from the particular bytes or carriers realizing it, and both guard against collapsing format change into content change.

layers.name: Instantiations and renditions
layers.description: Separate the intellectual record from each persistent inscription or format-specific realization, with format, extent, fixity and storage hints.

findings.name: Instantiation versus intellectual object
findings.description: RiC-CM treats Instantiation as distinct from Record Resource: the inscription on a carrier in a persistent recoverable form. PREMIS distinguishes intellectual entity, representation, file and bitstream, with format, size, creatingApplication, storage contentLocation and storageMedium. Dublin Core format is file format, physical medium or dimensions; hasFormat/isFormatOf relate equivalent content in another format. OAIS adds representation information so a designated community can interpret the object. A rendition is a format-specific realization of one content version; many renditions may exist without creating a new version. Storage location type and medium are recorded here; aisle/bin topology is out of scope.

data_elements.name: Instantiation identifier
data_elements.description: Typed identifier of the instantiation.

data_elements.name: PREMIS object category
data_elements.description: Object category: representation, file, bitstream or analogue.

data_elements.name: Media type
data_elements.description: IANA media type of the instantiation.

data_elements.name: Format registry name and key
data_elements.description: Format registry name and key for the instantiation format.

data_elements.name: Byte size
data_elements.description: Size of the instantiation in bytes.

data_elements.name: Storage medium
data_elements.description: Medium on which the instantiation is stored.

data_elements.name: Content location type and value
data_elements.description: Content location type and value for retrieval.

data_elements.name: Physical carrier description
data_elements.description: Description of the physical or analogue carrier.

artifacts.name: Content bitstream or physical carrier
artifacts.description: The recoverable inscription: digital bytes or a described analogue/physical carrier. Storage interface is a projection, not the semantics.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Instantiation identifier under the record identity; storage location is a hint, not identity.

questions.text: What instantiations or renditions currently realize this version, and what is each media type, format registry key, byte size and carrier?
answer_data: Array of instantiation objects with id, object-category (representation|file|bitstream|analogue), media-type, formatName/version or registry key, byte-size, carrier.

questions.text: Where is each instantiation located, on what medium, and is that location a content-address, URI, handle or physical place ref?
answer_data: contentLocationType, contentLocationValue, storageMedium, optional place ref; location is not identity.

questions.text: What representation information or creating application is required to present and interpret this instantiation?
answer_data: creatingApplication name/version/date; environment or representation-info refs; significant-properties list.

findings.name: Fixity and extent
findings.description: PREMIS fixity is messageDigestAlgorithm, messageDigest and optional originator, repeatable per file or bitstream. OAIS Preservation Description Information includes fixity to detect change. Dublin Core extent is size or duration. Fixity of an instantiation is not a version identifier, but a failed fixity check is an integrity event. Observation time of a checksum must be recorded separately from the event time of content creation.

data_elements.name: Message digest algorithm
data_elements.description: Algorithm that produced the stored digest.

data_elements.name: Message digest
data_elements.description: Digest value in hexadecimal or base64.

data_elements.name: Digest originator
data_elements.description: Agent reference for who or what originated the digest.

data_elements.name: Extent
data_elements.description: Declared extent as size or duration.

artifacts.name: Fixity block
artifacts.description: Stored digest(s) with algorithm, originator and computation timestamp.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Attached to the instantiation identifier with algorithm and computation timestamp.

questions.text: What is the authoritative checksum for each file or bitstream, which algorithm produced it, and who originated it?
answer_data: Array of {algorithm, digest, originator, computed-at RFC 3339}.

questions.text: When was fixity last verified, against which stored digest, and what was the outcome?
answer_data: Event: verified-at (observation time), digest compared, outcome (match|mismatch|not-run), verifier agent.

questions.text: What extent (bytes, pages, duration) is declared, and does it match the measured instantiation?
answer_data: Declared extent plus measured byte-size or duration; mismatch flag.

layers.name: Versioning and supersession
layers.description: Keep content states immutable once issued, and record which record or version replaces another.

findings.name: Immutable content versions
findings.description: Dublin Core hasVersion/isVersionOf cover versions, editions or adaptations with substantive content change, not mere format difference. PREMIS relationshipType/relationshipSubType plus relatedObjectIdentifier sequence versions and derivatives. Once a version is issued or captured, its content bytes are not overwritten; a later state is a new version with its own identifier, hash and event. Point-of-capture metadata that must not change is distinct from process metadata that accrues.

data_elements.name: Version identifier
data_elements.description: Typed identifier of the content version.

data_elements.name: Version number or label
data_elements.description: Human-facing version number or label.

data_elements.name: Version content hash
data_elements.description: Hash fixing the content state of the version.

data_elements.name: Version issued-at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 datetime at which the version was issued.

data_elements.name: Change note
data_elements.description: Note describing the substantive change in this version.

data_elements.name: Current version flag
data_elements.description: Whether this version is the current operative one.

artifacts.name: Version manifest
artifacts.description: Immutable listing of version id, content hash, issue time and predecessor.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Version identifier plus content hash; predecessor link orders the chain.

questions.text: Which version is current for use, and what is its content hash and issued-at time?
answer_data: version-id, content-hash, issued-at RFC 3339, is-current true.

questions.text: What is the ordered version chain, and which relationships are version-of versus format-of?
answer_data: Ordered list of version-ids with relationshipSubType (isVersionOf|hasFormat|derivedFrom) and sequence.

questions.text: Is in-place mutation of this version permitted, and if a correction is required what new version is issued?
answer_data: Boolean immutability rule; if correction, new version-id and change-note; erratum flag.

findings.name: Supersession between records
findings.description: Dublin Core replaces/isReplacedBy model a related resource that supplants another. A new record may supersede an older record (policy, specification, licence) without being a version of the same identity. Supersession does not by itself authorize destruction of the replaced record; disposition remains a separate control.

data_elements.name: Supersedes record ref
data_elements.description: Reference to an earlier record this record replaces.

data_elements.name: Superseded-by record ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the record that replaces this one.

data_elements.name: Supersession datetime
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 datetime from which supersession is effective.

artifacts.name: Supersession link
artifacts.description: Typed relation between two record identities with effective time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Pair of record identifiers plus effective time.

questions.text: Which earlier record(s) does this record replace, from when, and is the older identity retained?
answer_data: Array of {record-ref, effective-at RFC 3339, older-identity-retained boolean}.

questions.text: Has this record been replaced, and is it still retained under its schedule?
answer_data: superseded-by ref, effective-at, retention still in force boolean.

questions.text: Is the successor a new version of the same identity or a distinct record that replaces this one?
answer_data: Enum relation-kind: same-identity-version | distinct-record-replaces.

bundles.name: Authenticity and integrity
bundles.description: Explain why the record can be trusted as what it purports to be, complete and unaltered, including signatures, seals, timestamps, content credentials and the ISO authoritative-record characteristics.
bundles.rationale: Signature/seal/timestamp evidence and the assessed authoritative-record characteristics plus content credentials are grouped because they are the trust surface of the record, each binding to a named version or instantiation rather than to the abstract identity.

layers.name: Signatures, seals and timestamps
layers.description: Attach cryptographic or documentary authenticity evidence to a specific version or instantiation.

findings.name: Signatures, seals and timestamps
findings.description: PREMIS signatureInformation on file or bitstream includes signatureEncoding, signer, signatureMethod, signatureValue, signatureValidationRules, signatureProperties and keyInformation. eIDAS distinguishes simple, advanced and qualified electronic signatures; qualified electronic seals for legal persons; and qualified electronic time stamps with presumption of date/time accuracy and data integrity. A signature authenticates a specific version or instantiation, not the abstract identity in general. Validation status changes over time as certificates expire; validation events are distinct from signing events.

data_elements.name: Signer or sealer agent ref
data_elements.description: Agent reference for the signer or sealer.

data_elements.name: Signature method
data_elements.description: Signature method as a string or OID.

data_elements.name: eIDAS or equivalent level
data_elements.description: Enumerated assurance level such as simple, advanced or qualified.

data_elements.name: Signed-at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 datetime of signing.

data_elements.name: Trusted timestamp time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 datetime asserted by a trusted timestamp token.

data_elements.name: Current validity status
data_elements.description: Enumerated current validation status of the signature or seal.

data_elements.name: Signed version or instantiation ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the exact version or instantiation covered by the signature.

artifacts.name: Signature value and certificate chain
artifacts.description: The signature bytes or equivalent documentary seal image, plus certificate chain or seal evidence and optional qualified timestamp token.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the signed version or instantiation identifier together with the signer.

questions.text: Who signed or sealed which version or instantiation, by what method and at what time?
answer_data: signer-ref, signed-object-ref, method, signature-level, signed-at RFC 3339, optional timestamp-at from a TSA.

questions.text: What is the current validation status, when was it last validated, and against which rules?
answer_data: validity-status enum (valid|invalid|indeterminate|expired-cert|revoked); last-validated-at observation time; validation-rules ref; certificate-status.

questions.text: Is the evidence an individual signature, an organizational seal, a stamp, or a merely decorative image?
answer_data: Enum evidence-kind: qualified-signature | advanced-signature | simple-signature | qualified-seal | wet-ink | impressed-seal | decorative-nonbinding.

layers.name: Authoritative characteristics and content credentials
layers.description: Record ISO authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability claims, and optional C2PA-style bindings.

findings.name: Authoritative record characteristics
findings.description: ISO 23081 states that metadata must support assertions of integrity, authenticity, reliability and usability over time in business context. ISO 15489 requires records to remain authoritative through those characteristics: authentic (what it purports to be, created or sent by the purported agent at the purported time), reliable (trusted full and accurate content of the transaction), integrity (complete and unaltered), usable (locatable, retrievable, presentable, interpretable). These are assessed properties with evidence, not decorative flags.

data_elements.name: Authenticity assessment
data_elements.description: Structured assessment that the record is what it purports to be, with evidence.

data_elements.name: Reliability assessment
data_elements.description: Structured assessment of full and accurate content of the transaction.

data_elements.name: Integrity assessment
data_elements.description: Structured assessment that the record is complete and unaltered.

data_elements.name: Usability assessment
data_elements.description: Structured assessment that the record is locatable, retrievable, presentable and interpretable.

artifacts.name: Authoritativeness assessment note
artifacts.description: Recorded assessment with evidence refs (fixity, signature, custody, representation info) and assessment time. Pure assessment metadata may be inline if evidence artifacts live on related findings.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Record identity plus assessment time and evidence refs.

questions.text: Can this record be shown to be what it purports to be, created or sent by the purported agent at the purported time, and on what evidence?
answer_data: Boolean plus evidence refs (signature, custody event, register entry, C2PA manifest) and assessed-at RFC 3339.

questions.text: Has integrity been maintained (complete, unaltered since capture), and what unauthorized change if any was detected?
answer_data: integrity-status; last-fixity-outcome; missing-rendition flags; incident refs.

questions.text: Can the record still be located, retrieved, presented and interpreted by the intended community?
answer_data: locatable boolean, retrievable boolean, presentable boolean, interpretable boolean, representation-info-gap notes.

findings.name: Content credentials binding
findings.description: C2PA binds a signed manifest (assertions, claim, claim signature) to asset bytes via a hard binding (cryptographic hash of the asset or portion) and optional soft bindings (fingerprint or watermark). A standard manifest requires a hard binding. This is an emerging authenticity mechanism for digital media and generated content. It does not replace records capture, retention or legal-hold controls, and is not required for analogue records. Soft bindings are not statistically unique and must not be used as identity.

data_elements.name: C2PA manifest identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the active content-credential manifest.

data_elements.name: Hard-binding hash
data_elements.description: Cryptographic hash of the asset or portion binding the manifest to bytes.

data_elements.name: Soft-binding descriptor
data_elements.description: Fingerprint or watermark descriptor; a lookup hint, never identity.

data_elements.name: Claim generator
data_elements.description: Software or service that generated the claim.

artifacts.name: C2PA manifest store
artifacts.description: Embedded or sidecar manifest store (assertions, claim, claim signature) for the asset. Absent for most non-media records.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Manifest identifier bound to asset bytes by a hard binding; soft bindings are lookup hints only.

questions.text: Is a C2PA or equivalent content-credential manifest present, embedded or as sidecar, and does its hard binding match current bytes?
answer_data: present boolean; location (embedded|sidecar|remote); hard-binding match boolean; claim-generator.

questions.text: What origin, action or ingredient assertions does the active manifest claim?
answer_data: Array of assertion labels and summaries; ingredient manifest refs.

questions.text: If only a soft binding exists, is it being treated as identity or merely as a lookup hint?
answer_data: Enum use: lookup-hint | not-present | invalid-as-identity; policy note.

bundles.name: Provenance, custody and context
bundles.description: Record how the object came into existence, who has had custody, how it is registered, and how it relates to other records, agents and activities.
bundles.rationale: Lifecycle events and custody/register/relations are grouped because both answer where the record came from and who has been responsible for it, which is the evidence base for reliability under ISO 23081.

layers.name: Creation, capture and lifecycle events
layers.description: Distinguish business creation, records capture, preservation actions and the event times versus ingestion times.

findings.name: Creation and capture
findings.description: ISO 15489 separates creating records from capturing them in a records system. Capture, at minimum, assigns a unique identifier. Point-of-capture metadata should not change; process metadata accrues. Dublin Core created, issued, dateSubmitted, dateAccepted, modified and valid are distinct lifecycle dates. PREMIS events have eventType, eventDateTime, outcome, linking agents and objects. Event time of the business or records action must be stored separately from observation or ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Content created-at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 datetime at which the content was created.

data_elements.name: Captured-at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 datetime at which the object was captured as a record.

data_elements.name: Formally issued-at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 datetime of formal issue.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingested-at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 datetime at which the fact was observed or ingested into this system.

data_elements.name: Creator agent ref

findings.description: OAIS models movement as SIP at producer deposit, AIP in archival storage, and DIP at dissemination. PREMIS records ingest, migration, validation and similar events on objects. Migration and conversion are ISO 15489 processes that must not silently replace identity. Package role (sip|aip|dip) is a projection of the same intellectual record, not a second document.

layers.name: Custody, register and relations

findings.name: Custody and register
findings.description: Dublin Core provenance is a statement of changes in ownership and custody significant for authenticity, integrity and interpretation. RiC distinguishes the agent who creates a record from the agent who accumulates a record set. US practice transfers legal custody to the Archivist by instrument (SF 258) for permanent records. A custodial register entry (register ref, entry number, registered-at) anchors existence-level metadata without implying the registrar owns the record. Owner, creator, publisher, custodian and rights holder are different roles.

PREMIS relationship units link objects and events with sequence. RiC models membership of records in record sets and part/whole among record parts; the set itself is WM-REC-015. A record may contain nested records or record parts without becoming a fonds.

bundles.name: Retention, disposition and holds
bundles.description: Govern how long the record must be kept, under which authority, what happens at the end, and which holds or unscheduled status block destruction.
bundles.rationale: Retention/disposition and holds/exceptions are grouped because eligibility to destroy is computed from schedule facts and then vetoed by holds and unscheduled status; separating them would let a worklist present blocked records as destroyable.

layers.name: Retention and disposition
layers.description: Assign disposition authority, retention period, triggers including contingent events, and execute or evidence disposition.

findings.name: Retention authority and period
findings.description: ISO 15489 records controls include disposition authorities: minimum retention by class of records. 36 CFR 1220.18 defines retention period, disposition, disposition authority (US SF 115 approved by the Archivist or a GRS), series, temporary versus permanent, contingent records whose disposition depends on a future event, and unscheduled records that must be treated as permanent until scheduled. Trigger events (cutoff, closure, last action, property sale) start the clock; calendar arithmetic is a sibling. Assignment of a schedule is not execution of destruction.

findings.name: Disposition execution
findings.description: Disposition in 36 CFR is action taken on records no longer needed for current business. ISO 15489 includes disposition as a process. Execution must be blocked by active holds and by unscheduled status. Destruction of an instantiation is not destruction of the record if another authoritative instantiation remains; destruction of the record requires all instantiations and a disposition certificate or equivalent evidence. Transfer and accession are disposition actions that change custody rather than destroy content.

layers.name: Holds and exceptions

findings.name: Legal and administrative holds
findings.description: ISO 15489 requires protection from unauthorized destruction and authorized destruction only. 36 CFR treats unscheduled records as a standing freeze (treat as permanent). Operational legal holds (litigation, investigation, audit) are a widespread records-control pattern in ERM specifications (DoD 5015.02, MoReq) that were not retrieved as primary text in this run and are therefore recorded as an operating-surface finding with partial primary support from unauthorized-destruction protection and unscheduled-as-permanent rules. Holds override schedule eligibility until released; overlapping holds all must be released. A hold may cover content, metadata or both, and may extend to copies.

findings.name: Access conditions and marking
findings.description: ISO 15489 records controls include access and permission rules; access control is a clause-9 process using authorized rules. Dublin Core accessRights describes who may access the resource or its security status, including privacy and security restrictions. PREMIS rightsGranted.act and restriction plus term dates implement machine-actionable permissions. Default deny for content with metadata possibly more open is a common pattern but is a policy choice. Exceptions (redaction, privileged access, court order) must be explicit and auditable.

findings.description: PREMIS Rights include rightsBasis (copyright, licence, statute, other), jurisdiction, applicable dates, granted acts, restrictions and linking agents. Dublin Core rights, license, rightsHolder and dateCopyrighted describe rights held in the resource. Records rights (permission to read a government record) are not identical to intellectual-property rights to reproduce a work. Statute basis may both require retention and restrict disclosure.

findings.name: Certified copies and use events
findings.description: ISO 15489 includes use and reuse as a records process and requires authenticity to survive copies that are authorized. Dublin Core isFormatOf/hasFormat support extracts in another format. A certified copy is a new instantiation or even a new record with an attestation that it faithfully reproduces a named version; it is not a substitute for the original identity. Use events (view, print, download, disclose) are PREMIS-style events needed for audit.

composition.target: WM-REC-015 — archival fonds, collection or record set
composition.purpose: RiC Record Set and archival aggregations contain records; this model does not own fonds/series-as-set. Known candidate relation: WM-REC-015 CONTAINS WM-REC-001.
Creators, signers, custodial officers and requesters are agents; RiC Person/Position and PREMIS Agent are not duplicated here.

composition.target: world.organization — issuing organization, corporate custodian, rights holder
composition.purpose: Issuer, owner and archival institution are organizations or corporate bodies described elsewhere.
Document numbers, register identifiers and objectIdentifierType values must come from governed schemes.
Retention trigger arithmetic, working-day cutoffs and timezone-normalised RFC 3339 values depend on the time model.
A message envelope is not a record identity; bodies and attachments that are captured resolve to records in this model.
RiC Activity and ISO business classification link a record to the work that produced it; the activity master is sibling data.
Coverage spatial, rights jurisdiction, and physical custody place refs belong to a place model; storageMedium here is not a gazetteer.

composition.target: world.access-policy — access and permission rule engine
composition.purpose: ISO 15489 access and permission rules are authored as controls elsewhere; this model stores the assignment and the decision event.

composition.target: world.legal-matter — litigation, investigation or audit matter
composition.purpose: Holds point at a matter; the docket is not a property of the record. Primary hold-matter standard was not retrieved; link is operational.
Descriptive facet on every document; mix-in, not a replacement for records controls.
Lifecycle, controls and authoritative-record characteristics. Alignment only; no conformance claim.
Event-capable metadata demonstrating authenticity, integrity, reliability and usability. RiC-CM itself notes remaining entity-model differences.
Object/event/agent/rights semantics for preservation, fixity, format and signatures.
Record versus Instantiation versus Record Set split; this model aligns to Record and Instantiation only.
SIP/AIP/DIP and PDI categories as package projections of a record, not a second identity.
Optional hard-bound manifest for digital media origin; emerging, not required for all records.

composition.target: eidas-trust-services — eIDAS signatures, seals and timestamps
composition.purpose: Regional legal effect of electronic signatures, seals and qualified timestamps on a version.
Jurisdiction-specific record/nonrecord/unscheduled/permanent definitions used as an alignment, not a global default.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension declares the jurisdiction whose record definition applies; US 36 CFR / 44 U.S.C. definitions apply only when US Federal jurisdiction is asserted.
The adopting Dimension declares whether eIDAS signature levels apply, i.e. whether EU/EEA trust-service law governs signatures, seals and timestamps.
The adopting Dimension supplies the UUID or ULID fallback identifier and the governed schemes used for master and public identifiers.
The adopting Dimension supplies an explicit normalization policy where local records law still uses date-only cutoffs, rather than inferring times.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Master identifiers, register identifiers and PREMIS objectIdentifierType values come from governed schemes owned by the naming sibling; filenames, URL paths and object-storage keys are location hints and are never used as namespace identity.
registry_links: WM-REC-015 — archival fonds, collection or record set that contains records
world.identifier-naming — identifier scheme registry supplying schemes for master and public identifiers

canonicalization_rules: Timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; event time is stored separately from ingestion or observation time.
Identity is canonicalized as a typed scheme plus value; storage URLs, filenames and paths are never canonicalized into the identifier.
Version-of, format-of and instantiation relations are kept distinct rather than collapsed into a single file field.
patch_rules: Adding a version, rendition, signature, hold or register entry is a create of a child object, not an overwrite of the parent identity.
Issued content bytes are replaced only by issuing a successor version with its own identifier, hash and change note.
Forbidden patches: in-place edit of issued content bytes, silent identifier change, and back-dating capture without an explicit correction event.
compatibility_rules: Alignments to ISO 15489/23081, PREMIS, RiC-CM, DCMI, OAIS, C2PA and eIDAS are mappings only; no conformance is claimed without a mapped profile.
Jurisdiction-specific fields such as US unscheduled/permanent status and eIDAS signature levels apply only when the adopting Dimension asserts that jurisdiction.
Overlapping entity models (PREMIS Intellectual Entity, RiC Record, DCMI resource, OAIS Content Information) are mapped, not merged.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier in a named scheme
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
A date is not an identifier; filename, URL path and storage key are location hints, not identity
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Dates are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and event time is stored separately from ingestion time.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serially issued artifacts — register entries, version manifests, disposition certificates, hold notices, access decision records and certified copies — are named by the master record identifier plus their own entry number, version label or certificate number; the serial never replaces the master identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: An issued content version is immutable; identity is independent of storage location and filename; point-of-capture metadata does not silently change; disposition cannot execute while any hold is active or while the record is unscheduled where that jurisdiction so requires; destroying one instantiation does not destroy the record identity if another authoritative instantiation remains; dates are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and event time is stored separately from ingestion time.

policies: Capture assigns a unique identifier before the object is treated as a record under controls.
Content bytes of an issued version are replaced only by issuing a successor version.
Default deny content access; metadata may be separately authorized; every content disclosure writes a use event.
Retention assignment is mandatory for captured records; unscheduled US Federal records are ineligible for destruction.
Legal and administrative holds overlay and block disposition until every applicable hold is released.
Owner grants access; custodian or registrar may operate the store without acquiring ownership.
Authenticity evidence (signature, seal, timestamp, C2PA, fixity) always names the signed version or instantiation.
Certified copies bind to a named source version hash and do not overwrite the source identity.

read: Return register-level metadata only when the requester is not authorized for content.
Return an evidentiary package (version chain, signatures, custody, fixity) only under the evidentiary access scope.
Never treat a storage URL as the identifier in API responses.
create: Create is capture or first registration: mint master identifier, freeze point-of-capture metadata, record created-at and ingested-at separately.
Adding a version, rendition, signature, hold or register entry is a create of a child object, not an overwrite of the parent identity.
update: Mutable: descriptive labels, current-version pointer, current custodian, current marking, schedule assignment, validity-status of signatures.
Forbidden: in-place edit of issued content bytes, silent identifier change, back-dating capture without an explicit correction event.
delete: There is no silent delete. Destruction is execute-disposition after eligibility and hold checks.
A destruction stub (identity, class, disposed-at, authority, evidence ref) is retained as required by local law.
Delete of a working copy instantiation is not record destruction unless it is the last copy and authority exists.

roles.name: Hold administrator
responsibilities: Place and release legal or administrative holds
Scope holds to content, metadata and copies as required
Ensure overlapping holds are independently tracked

roles.name: Requester / user
responsibilities: Not treat a dissemination copy as the preservation master

access.default_rule: Deny content and evidentiary packages; allow existence-level register metadata only where the applied access-rights statement marks it public; owner or an authorized policy engine may grant broader scopes.
exceptions: Court order, warrant or statutory disclosure duty
Redacted dissemination DIP that omits exempt passages
Privileged attorney-client or personnel content visible only to named roles
Disability or accessibility reformatting that must not be treated as a new original
Emergency vital-records retrieval logged after the fact within a defined SLA
audit_requirements: Log capture, version issue, signature, register, classify, hold place/release, access decision, use, migration and disposition with agent, event time and ingestion time.
Retain access and disposition logs at least as long as the record or as required by the audit schedule, whichever is longer.
Fixity failures and signature invalidations raise integrity incidents linked to the object.

coverage.claim: This result is a defensible, format-neutral operating model of a governed document/record grounded in ISO records-management and metadata standards, ICA RiC-CM, PREMIS, DCMI, OAIS, US Federal records definitions, C2PA and eIDAS guidance. It is not a claim of universal completeness or of conformance to any of those instruments.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier, scheme, public IRI and Dimension UUID/ULID priority; dates excluded as identifiers.
Create, capture, issue, register, classify, migrate, use, hold, dispose; document-versus-record status.
Part/whole, format-of, version-of, replaces, references, requires, source, membership in WM-REC-015 record sets.
RFC 3339 event versus ingestion times; created, issued, captured, valid, trigger, hold, disposition datetimes.
Custody chain, PREMIS events, OAIS PDI provenance, DC provenance, C2PA assertions as optional.
Owner versus custodian versus rights holder versus creator; registrar does not acquire ownership.
Fixity, signature validation, C2PA hard-binding match, authoritativeness assessments.
Marking, access-rights, PREMIS rightsGranted, default deny content, exceptions and use events.
Disposition authority, triggers, contingent and unscheduled, holds, destruction evidence, last-copy rule.
Alignments to ISO 15489/23081, PREMIS, RiC-CM, DCMI, OAIS, C2PA, eIDAS, 36 CFR; mix-in versus align versus reference distinguished.
ISO characteristics; signatures, seals, timestamps; C2PA marked emerging.
Assignment of business class and documentary form; scheme authoring out of scope.
Instantiation versus intellectual object; format registry, media type, representation info.
Operating surface included; DoD 5015.02 and MoReq hold schemas not retrieved as primary text.
contentLocation and storageMedium in-scope; facilities topology out of scope.

known_omissions: MoReq2010 / Modular Requirements for Records Systems not fetched as primary text.
DoD 5015.02-STD Electronic Records Management Software Application Design Criteria not fetched.
ISO 16175 (records in business systems), ISO 14641 (electronic archiving) and ISO 17068 (trusted third party repository) not fetched.
ISO 19005 PDF/A, METS, BagIt (RFC 8493) and PRONOM/DROID as format-identification practice not modelled in depth.
EDRM / FRCP 37(e) litigation-hold primary texts not fetched; holds rest on ISO unauthorized-destruction protection plus 36 CFR unscheduled freeze.
Vital records / business-continuity copies, encrypted or DRM-inhibited objects (PREMIS inhibitors) only lightly touched.
Database, GIS and other dynamic system-of-record snapshots as records: in ISO 15489 scope by principle, under-specified here.
Spoken, audiovisual and 3D records beyond Instantiation/format.
National variants beyond US CFR, eIDAS and JIS identical adoption (e.g. Australian Archives Act, UK TNA, China GB/T 18894) not retrieved.
Blockchain or distributed-register identity as an emerging identifier class not given primary support.
conflicts: ISO 15489 treats aggregations as records under the same principles; RiC-CM insists a Record Set is a different entity from a Record. This model sides with RiC for aggregations (WM-REC-015) and ISO for capture-as-record lifecycle.
PREMIS Intellectual Entity versus RiC Record versus DCMI BibliographicResource versus OAIS Content Information are overlapping but not identical; mapped, not merged.
US 44 U.S.C. 3301 record definition is jurisdiction-specific and excludes extra copies and exhibit materials; ISO 15489 has no such Federal-record test.
eIDAS qualified signature legal effect does not automatically apply outside the EU; C2PA trust does not equal eIDAS qualification.
Version (content change) versus rendition/format (hasFormat) versus Instantiation (carrier) are frequently collapsed in ECM products.
Owner, custodian, rights holder and creator are often stored as a single 'author' field in implementations; standards distinguish them.
Data-subject erasure (e.g. GDPR Art. 17, not fetched as primary here) can conflict with authorized retention; surfaced as an unresolved rights question rather than a default destroy.
C2PA hard binding and PREMIS fixity both hash bytes but serve different trust frameworks and must not be treated as interchangeable certificates.
regional_assumptions: ISO 15489/23081 and RiC-CM are treated as the international backbone.
US 36 CFR/44 U.S.C. definitions apply only when the adopting Dimension asserts US Federal jurisdiction.
eIDAS signature levels apply when the adopting Dimension asserts EU/EEA trust-service law.
C2PA is optional and currently most relevant to media and generated-content assets in adopting markets.
Language of description defaults to the record's content language; multilingual titles are allowed via localized strings.
RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset or Z are required even where local records law still uses date-only cutoffs; date-only values should be normalized with an explicit policy, not inferred.
adversarial_checks: Would a filename, object-storage key or 'document date' be accepted as the master identifier? The model forbids it; identity finding requires a typed scheme.
Would converting PDF to PDF/A mint a new record identity or only a rendition? Format-of versus version-of is an explicit question; conversion is a migration event.
Would deleting the last working copy while a preservation AIP remains be logged as record destruction? Last-copy and package-role questions block that collapse.
Would a C2PA soft binding or watermark be used as the record id? Explicitly forbidden; soft bindings are lookup hints.
Would releasing one of two overlapping holds authorize destruction? Remaining-active-hold-ids must be empty.
Would a custodian's register rights be treated as ownership or as a right to grant public access? Stewardship and access default_rule keep owner as grantor.
Would an unscheduled US Federal record appear on a destroy worklist? Unscheduled-treat-as-permanent is a first-class status.
Would a certified extract that omits annexes keep the original record id? Certified-copy finding forces a same-identity versus new-extract choice.
